hits.text:
Feels like we're out of short-term narratives why crypto can pump.

Sure, there's institutional adoption but they get most of upside without buying our coins. 

Thus betting on that adoption via tokens is meh: upside seems to be in equity or private markets. 

Crypto was supposed to solve this!

Worse, seems that many crypto tokens are here to pay for institutional partnerships instead of accruing value to them. We're exit liquidity here.

HYPE got the NYSE news and now the trade played out. Currently waiting for all licenses and see how much it affects buybacks.

AVAX partnership will 'provide core ledger technology for NYSE' but what does that mean for the token?

Cosmos ATOM provided core ledger technology for shitloads of companies and they are basically dead.

BTC would pump if there was money printing in sight but that won't happen until AI bubble collapses:

and that would first rekt crypto as well. 

(I would've thought differently but AI crashing and rebounded while crypto crashed without rebound is making us all bearish).

Meanwhile trenches are rekt beyond believe. Pump, FOMO & grifters are running out of dumb money and backlash on X is getting louder.

Mid to long term it's clear that crypto is here to stay.

But we'll be tested by 1) democrats getting their vandetta on crypto and 2) interest rates increasing that can't be good for risk assets.

The most bullish point about this post is that it sounds so bearish, and usually when one wants to sell is the best time to buy?

Crypto still looks attractive for asymmetric trades.

No need to hold 100% of your net worth in crypto like BTC or ETH.

For me, it's something like $TRUE for challenging Polymarket and $BP for next big CEX+tokenization trade.

We had $ZEC and $HYPE that were relatively 'easy' trades if you were following CT.

Chasing those trades is fun and I will stay in crypto for it.

But my time of 100% allocating to crypto is behind.

this is the most difficult part of running a remote team

working remotely is great, but you have to make the effort to check on people

As a VC, I consider this a very positive signal.

Instead of force-feeding my agent excel sheets, PDFs, and screenshots of charts, I can hand it one artifact that compresses everything I should know about your business.

What it tells me: 
1) You respect my time. I can debate, discuss, and probe your business before we meet, so we can skip the "wait, wtf are you doing?" part and get straight to the heart of what you're building.
2) You understand how investors work now.
3) You're AI-native.
4) You're not afraid of a neutral read on your company. My AI will give me that anyway, the only question is whether you'll make me do more steps in between to get there.

One warning: I will ask my AI how biased your company.md was, and if there's anything in there that feels misleading. The more objective, the better.

This should become the gold standard for fundraising.
